body:
The proper solution to this problem is to chunk the protobuf message into smaller messages (say 4KiB). We are on a very old version of gRPC and since then gRPCs default max message size has been decreased to a saner 4MiB. 

The main problem with very large message sizes is that the whole message needs to eventually be reconstructed in memory. Lot's of buffering overhead internally in gRPC and also (moving) garbage collectors very much dislike objects/byte[] sized >100MiB.
We're already chunking protobuf messages, aren't we? Maybe the server-side isn't chunking, because our upload code path is chunking, unless I'm misremembering.
I think this is a bug in remote_worker, not Bazel as such.
Sorry, I already have a fix for this, I will send it out for review shortly (need to get some prerequisites in).

I SSH'd into the machine and the file is there and can be read fine:

The only thing I noticed is that the bazelrc file has no newline at the end, but I doubt that'd trip up `blaze_util::ReadFile`.

I suspect this failure is a flake.

issue.title: WIP: investigating inconsistent tests

repository.name: mu-scala
repository.description: Mu is a purely functional library for building RPC endpoint based services with support for RPC and HTTP/2

issue.body:
# WIP: do not merge

Hey, after testing locally a bit, I've seen that what makes the test fail is that the parameter received in [`biStreaming`](https://github.com/frees-io/freestyle-rpc/blob/master/modules/server/src/test/scala/fs2/Utils.scala#L130-L134) method comes empty some times, and that makes the flatmap fail fast and return the empty stream (which later is materialized to an empty list on the client.)

I'll be conducting some tests in this branch, and updating the description of the PR with my findings, but seems that avoiding that flatmap make most test pass.

---

Currently I'm facing two different errors:

## 1. GRPC error

this one I've been able to replicate it by just executing the tests with a `sbt server/tests` (maybe a couple of times, in travis seems to occur more likely).

`INTERNAL: Failed to frame message`

There are apparently other occurences of that error in the internets:

https://github.com/grpc/grpc-java/issues/1629
https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/2822

This one seems to be related with the size of the frame

## 2. Netty error

this one can be replicated with:


There are comments suggesting that this issue may be related to message frame size too... I'll try to investigate in that area.
